 \section{Polynomials and the low-degree code}
 % Paper label sec:ld-encoding kept for cross-reference fidelity.
 \label{sec:ld-encoding}
 
 \begin{definition}[Individual and total degree]\label{def:polynomials-degree}
 	\uses{def:polyfunc}
 	An $m$-variate polynomial $f$ over $\F_q$ is a function of the form
 	\[
 		f(x_1, \dots, x_m) = \sum_{\alpha \in \{0, 1, \dots, q-1\}^m}
 		c_\alpha\, x_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots x_m^{\alpha_m}
 	\]
 	with coefficients $c_\alpha \in \F_q$; the coefficients are uniquely
 	determined by $f$, since the $q^m$ monomial functions indexed by
 	$\alpha \in \{0, 1, \dots, q-1\}^m$ span the $q^m$-dimensional space of all
 	functions $\F_q^m \to \F_q$ and are therefore linearly independent. The
 	polynomial $f$ has \emph{individual degree (at most) $d$} if
 	$c_\alpha \neq 0$ only when $\alpha_i \le d$ for all $1 \le i \le m$, and
 	\emph{total degree (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha \neq 0$ only when
 	$\sum_i \alpha_i \le d$. (Affine) \emph{multilinear} polynomials are those
 	of individual degree $1$.
 	% Relationship to def:polyfunc: polyfunc keeps polynomial representatives,
 	% so evaluation identifies it with the function classes above only for
 	% d <= q-1.
 	Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc} introduces the set $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ of
 	polynomials in $\F_q[x_1, \dots, x_m]$ of degree at most $d$ in each
 	variable, identified by their polynomial representatives rather than by the
 	functions they induce. Evaluation maps $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ onto the set of
 	$m$-variate polynomials of individual degree at most $\min(d, q-1)$ in the
 	sense above; for $d \le q-1$ this map is a bijection, while for $d \ge q$
 	distinct representatives, such as $x_1^q$ and $x_1$, induce the same
 	function. Statements phrased in terms of $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ retain the
 	representative convention of Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}.
 \end{definition}
 
 \begin{lemma}[Schwartz--Zippel lemma~\cite{Sch80,Zip79}]\label{lem:schwartz-zippel}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.schwartzZippel_totalDegree}
+	\leanok
 	% Restatement of lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree under the source's label.
 	\uses{def:polynomials-degree}
 	Let $f, g : \F_q^m \to \F_q$ be two unequal polynomials of total degree at
 	most $d$. Then
 	\[
 		\Prb_{\bx \sim \F_q^m}[f(\bx) = g(\bx)] \le \frac{d}{q}\;.
 	\]
 \end{lemma}
 \begin{proof}
+	\leanok
 	\uses{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}
 	This is Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}, stated and proved in
 	Chapter~\ref{chap:preliminaries}; it is restated here under the label used
 	by \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}.
 \end{proof}
 
 \begin{remark}\label{rem:schwartz-zippel-restated}
 	Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel} restates the total-degree bound of
 	Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree} under the label used by
 	\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The individual-degree consequence,
 	Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-individual}, shows that distinct elements of
 	$\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ agree on at most an $md/q$ fraction of the points of
 	$\F_q^m$; the analysis of the Pauli basis test uses the bound in this
 	individual-degree form.
 \end{remark}
 
 The Schwartz--Zippel lemma implies that low-degree polynomials form an
 error-correcting code with good distance, the \emph{low-degree code} (a special
 case of the generalized Reed--Muller code).
 
 \begin{definition}[Low-degree encoding]\label{def:low-degree-encoding}
 	\uses{def:polynomials-degree}
 	Fix an integer $m \in \N$ and let $M = 2^m$. For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$
 	define the $m$-variate multilinear polynomial over $\F_q$
 	\[
 		\mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(x)
 		= \prod_{i : y_i = 1} x_i \cdot \prod_{i : y_i = 0} (1 - x_i)\;,
 	\]
 	identifying $\{0,1\}$ with a subset of $\F_q$. Restricted to the subcube
 	$\{0,1\}^m$, the polynomial $\mathrm{ind}_{m,y}$ vanishes everywhere except
 	at $x = y$, where it equals $1$. For $a \in \F_q^M$, label the coordinates
 	of $a$ as $a_y$ for $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ (identifying $\{0,1\}^m$ with
 	$\{1, \dots, M\}$ by the lexicographic ordering). The \emph{low-degree
 	encoding of $a$} is the multilinear polynomial $g_a : \F_q^m \to \F_q$,
 	% Paper equation label kept on the display it names.
 	\begin{equation}\label{eq:ld-encoding}
 		g_a(x) = \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} a_y \cdot \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(x)\;.
 	\end{equation}
 	For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ one has $g_a(y) = a_y$, and $g_a$ has total
 	degree at most $m$.
 \end{definition}
 
 \begin{definition}[Indicator vector and linearity of the encoding]\label{def:indicator-vector}
 	\uses{def:low-degree-encoding, def:dot-product-orthogonal}
 	For $x \in \F_q^m$, the \emph{indicator vector} is
 	\[
 		\mathrm{ind}_m(x)
 		= \bigl(\mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(x)\bigr)_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} \in \F_q^M\;.
 	\]
 	With this notation the low-degree encoding satisfies, for every
 	$a \in \F_q^M$ and $x \in \F_q^m$,
 	% Paper equation label kept on the display it names.
 	\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}
 		g_a(x) = a \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(x)\;;
 	\end{equation}
 	in particular the map $a \mapsto g_a$ is $\F_q$-linear.
 \end{definition}

 \begin{definition}[Lines]\label{def:line}

 	\begin{equation}\label{eq:line-set}

 	is explicitly allowed, in which case the line is the singleton $\{u\}$. A

 	vector of $\F_q^m$; such a line is said to be \emph{parallel to the $i$-th
 	direction}. A line $\ell(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists
 	$i \in \{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$ such that $v_1 = v_2 = \dots = v_i = 0$ (for
 	$i = 0$ the condition is vacuous, so every line is diagonal).

       Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))

    31	  Cube P.m × Fin P.model.basisDim → ZMod 2

    33	/-- The ideal auxiliary state tensored with the qubit EPR register, in the
    34	local-player ordering used by `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
    35	noncomputable def idealQubitState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    36	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    37	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    38	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    39	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
    40	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    41	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv
    42	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    43	    (fun p =>

    45	        (EuclideanSpace.equiv (QubitRegister P × QubitRegister P) ℂ

    62	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P)

    68	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq

    70	/-- Alice's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
    71	noncomputable def qubitProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)

   102	/-- Lift a conjugated Bob effect to the full qubit target space. -/
   103	noncomputable def liftedQubitBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}

   111	
   112	/-- Alice's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   113	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceA
   114	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   115	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=

   117	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   118	      (liftedQubitAEffect S w.φA

   123	/-- Bob's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   124	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceB
   125	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   126	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   127	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   128	    ‖applyOperatorToState

   130	          ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   131	        qubitProjOnB'' P W u)

   133	
   134	/-- `cor:pauli-binary`: soundness of the Pauli basis test in qubit
   135	coordinates. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:430-454`, paper
   136	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1491`.
   137	
   138	The theorem retains the source-compatible nonnegative error boundary and uses

   140	theorem pauli_soundness_qubit :
   141	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧

   149	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   150	            ∀ W : PauliKind,
   151	              qubitOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤
   152	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q := by

   155	end

   120	/-- A simultaneous tuple of `L.k` bounded polynomial representatives. -/
   121	noncomputable abbrev PolyTuple (L : LdParams) :=
   122	  Fin L.k → PolyIndex L.m (ScalarQ L) L.d
   123	
   124	/-- The constant-family specialization used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
   125	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasTuple (L : LdParams) (ι : Type*)
   126	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   127	  PolyMeasFamily L.k (fun _ => ScalarQ L) (fun _ => L.m) (fun _ => L.d) ι
   128	
   129	/-- Evaluate every component of a polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   130	def evalPolyTupleAt {L : LdParams} (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
   131	    (g : PolyTuple L) : Fin L.k → ScalarQ L :=
   132	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   133	
   134	/-- Embed a geometric point into the ambient coefficient space used by a
   135	point question. -/
   136	def pointSpaceOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdSpace L :=
   137	  fun i => match i with
   138	  | .inl (.inl j) => u j
   139	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   140	  | .inr _ => 0
   141	
   142	/-- The typed low-degree point question associated with `u`. -/
   143	def ldPointQuestionOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdQuestion L :=
   144	  (.point, pointSpaceOf L u)
   145	
   146	/-- Read the point component of a low-degree answer, sending answers of the
   147	wrong form to the fixed zero tuple. This total relabeling turns the strategy's
   148	answer measurement into the point POVM used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
   149	def ldPointValuesOrZero (L : LdParams) : LdAnswer L → Fin L.k → ScalarQ L
   150	  | .pointVals values => values
   151	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   152	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   153	
   154	/-- The quantitative error function in `lem:ld-soundness`.  Its argument order
   155	is `(a, b, ε, q, m, d, k)`. -/
   156	noncomputable def deltaLd (a b ε : ℝ) (q m d k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   157	  a * Real.rpow (((d * m * k : ℕ) : ℝ)) a *
   158	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
   159	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
   160

   162	test (`lem:ld-soundness`, blueprint lines 135--160; paper theorem and proof
   163	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`).

   180	                  heteroKron
   181	                    (((S.A (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
   182	                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome) 1)
   183	                (fun u outcome =>
   184	                  heteroKron 1
   185	                    ((GB.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))

   187	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))

   191	                (fun u outcome =>
   192	                  heteroKron 1
   193	                    (((S.B (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
   194	                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome))

   196	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   197	                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
   198	                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.
   455	
   456	To conclude it remains to extend the result to the case of general $\ldc$. This is done 
   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

   612	The following theorem records the self-testing (also known as \emph{rigidity})
   613	properties of the Magic Square game.
   614	Its self-testing properties
   615	are crucial to the Pauli basis test.
   616	In particular, it is used to enforce anticommutation relations between certain
   617	pairs of operators.
   618	We will refer to this theorem in the proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test (\Cref{thm:pauli} below) in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}.
   619	
   620	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]
   621	  \label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   622	
   623	
   624	Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ with probability $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ is a state. Then there exist local isometries $\phi_A: \mH_A \to \mH_{A'} \otimes \mH_{A''},\phi_B: \mH_B \to \mH_{B'} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ (where $\mH_{A'},\mH_{B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\otimes 2}$ and $\mH_{A''},\mH_{B''}$ are finite dimensional) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{A''} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ such that 
   625	\begin{enumerate}
   626	    \item $\left \| \phi_A \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2} \otimes \ket{\aux} \right \| \leq O(\sqrt{\eps})$,
   627	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have that
   628	    \begin{gather*}
   629	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^X_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   630	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^Z_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   631	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^X_b)_{B'} \\
   632	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^Z_b)_{B'}
   633	    \end{gather*}
   634	    where the $\approx_{\sqrt{\eps}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}_{A'B'} \otimes \ket{\aux}_{A''B''}$ and the answer summation is over $b \in \{0,1\}$. As a consequence, letting 
   635	    \begin{gather*}
   636	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_1 \\
   637	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_1 \\
   638	    \end{gather*}
   639	    it holds that
   640	    \begin{gather*}
   641	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} \otimes I_{B' B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \otimes I_{B' B''} \\
   642	        I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \;,
   643	      \end{gather*}
   644	      where the notation $M \approx_{\delta} N$ for $M, N$ that are not POVM
   645	      elements means
   646	      \[  \bra{\psi} (M-N)^\dagger (M-N) \ket{\psi}  \leq  O(\delta). \]
   647	\end{enumerate}

   649	\end{theorem}
   650	\begin{proof}
   651	 	A proof of the rigidity of the Magic Square game can be found in~\cite[Theorem 6.9]{coladangelo2017robust}. There are a couple minor differences between their rigidity statement and the one stated here. First, they state that the robustness of the Magic Square self-test is $O(\eps)$; however they specify the closeness between the actual and ideal states in terms of the trace norm, whereas we specify the closeness between $\phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi}$ and $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}\otimes \ket{\aux}$ in terms of the Euclidean distance, which translates to $O(\sqrt{\eps})$ instead of $O(\eps)$. Second, their choice of ideal strategy specifies that the observables corresponding to $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$ questions are $I \otimes \sigma^Z$ and $\sigma^{Z} \sigma^{X} \otimes \sigma^Z \sigma^X$; however under a local change of basis these are equivalent to $\sigma^X \otimes I$ and $\sigma^Z \otimes I$ respectively.
   652	\end{proof}

  1426	\paragraph{Soundness of the Pauli basis test.} 
  1427	We state the soundness properties of the Pauli basis test.
  1428	The following is an adaptation of the self-testing statement in~\cite[Theorem
  1429	6.4]{NW19}.

  1431	\begin{theorem}
  1432	  \label{thm:pauli}
  1433	There exists a function 
  1434	\[\delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})\]
  1435	 for universal constants $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$ such that the following holds. For all admissible parameter tuples $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ and for all strategies $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeed with probability at least $1 - \eps$, there exist local isometries $\phi_\alice: \mH_\alice \to \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\alice''},\phi_\bob: \mH_\bob \to \mH_{\bob'} \otimes \mH_{\bob''}$ (where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ and $\mH_{\alice''},\mH_{\bob''} \cong (\C^q)^{\otimes M}$ with $M = 2^m$) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\bob'}$ such that 
  1436	\begin{enumerate}
  1437	    \item $\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}  \right \| \leq \delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q)$,
  1438	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
  1439	    \begin{gather*}
  1440	        \tilde{A}^{(\pauli,W)}_u \otimes I_{\bob'\bob''} \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} (\tau^W_u)_{\alice''} \otimes I_{\alice' \bob' \bob''} \\
  1441	        I_{\alice'\alice''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{(\pauli,W)}_u    \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} I_{\alice' \alice'' \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_u)_{\bob''}\;,
  1442	    \end{gather*}
  1443	    where the $\approx_{\delta_{\qld}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice'\bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}_{\alice''\bob''}$ and the answer summation is over $u \in \F_q^M$.

  1503	\begin{definition}[Canonical parameters of the Pauli basis test]
  1504	  \label{def:introparams}
  1505	  Let $a,b$ be the universal constants specified in Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
  1506	  Let $c$ denote the smallest even integer that is at least $(b + a)/b$.
  1507	  For all integers $R \geq 4$, define the tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$
  1508	  where
  1509	  \begin{itemize}
  1510	  	\item $q = 2^k$ for $k = c \lceil  \log \log R  \rceil + 1$.
  1511		\item $m = 2^j$ where $2^j \leq c \lceil \log R \rceil + 1 < 2^{j+1}$. 
  1512		\item $d = 1$. 
  1513	  \end{itemize}
  1514	\end{definition}
  1515	
  1516	Intuitively, this choice of parameters is such that the Pauli basis test
  1517	certifies the presence of an $M=2^m$-qudit EPR state (of local dimension $q$), or
  1518	equivalently an $M\log q$-qubit EPR state.
  1519	
  1520	\begin{lemma}
  1521	  \label{lem:delta-bound}
  1522	 For all integers $R \geq 4$, the parameter tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$ is
  1523	  admissible (see Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), satisfies $2^m \geq R$, and furthermore there exist
  1524	  universal constants $a'\geq 1$ and $0 < b' \leq 1$ such that the function
  1525	  $\delta_\qld(\eps, m, d, q)$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} is at most
  1526	   \[
  1527	   	a' ( \log(R)^{a'} \cdot \eps^{b'} + \log(R)^{-b'}) \;.
  1528		\]
  1529	\end{lemma}

  1531	\begin{proof}
  1532	  We verify the admissibility of $\introparams(R)$ first: the field size $q =
  1533	  2^k$ is admissible because $k$ is odd. We have $m | q$ because for all $R \geq 4$ we have  
  1534	  \[
  1535	  	2^j \leq 2 c \lceil \log R \rceil \leq 2 \log^c R \leq 2^k~.
  1536	  \]
  1537		Next, we show that $R \leq 2^m$. Since $m = 2^j \geq (c/2) \log R$, we have that
  1538		\[
  1539			2^m \geq R^{c/2} \geq R
  1540		\]
  1541		where we used that $c \geq 2$. 
  1542	
  1543	Finally, we show the desired bound on the error function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. First, observe that $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$ because $k \leq m$.
  1544	  Note that for $R \geq 2$, we have $m \leq 2c \log R$, and furthermore $q =
  1545	  2^k \geq \log^c R$.

  1549	    & = a (md)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}) \tag{by Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}}  \\
  1550	    & \leq a (md)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$}  \\
  1551	    & = a (m)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $d=1$}  \\
  1552	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $m \leq 2c \log R$}\\
  1553	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2(\log R)^{-cb}) \tag{because  $q \geq \log^c R$}\\
  1554	    & \leq 2a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-cb}) \\
  1555	    & = 2a (2c)^a ( (\log R)^{a}\eps^{b} + (\log R)^{a-cb}) \\
  1556	    & \leq 2a(2c)^{a} \left ( (\log R)^{a} \eps^{b}
  1557	      + (\log R)^{-b} \right) \tag{because  $cb - a \geq b \geq 0$}\\
  1558	    & \leq a' ( (\log R)^{a'} \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-b}),
  1559	  \end{align*}
  1560	  where $a'$ is defined as the quantity $2a(2c)^a$.

  1562	\end{proof}

1	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.Polynomials

     3	/-!
     4	# The low-degree encoding
     5	
     6	This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials
     7	and packages the resulting low-degree code as honest polynomial representatives.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The source-facing nodes are `def:polynomials-degree`,
    12	`def:low-degree-encoding`, and `def:indicator-vector` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:321-417`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    15	The polynomial class `def:polyfunc` is reused from
    16	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` (the LDT formalization).
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	open MvPolynomial
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/
    25	/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
    26	type in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint
    27	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    29	-/
    30	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool
    31	
    32	/--
    33	The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and
    34	zero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in
    35	`def:low-degree-encoding` (blueprint lines 381-401; paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    39	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    40	  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)
    41	
    42	/--
    43	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    44	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
    45	functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`; paper origin:
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    50	    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    51	  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y
    52	
    53	/- Evaluation shorthand for the representative polynomial in
    54	`def:low-degree-encoding`; it is Lean-only notation. -/
    55	/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    60	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=
    61	  eval x (lowDegreeEncoding a)
    62	
    63	/--
    64	The indicator vector `ind_m(x)` of `def:indicator-vector`.
    65	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`; paper origin:
    66	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    67	-/
    68	noncomputable def indicatorVec {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    69	    (x : Fin m → K) : Cube m → K :=
    70	  fun y => eval x (indicatorPoly y)
    71	
    72	/--
    73	The defining dot-product identity for the encoding, corresponding to
    74	Equation `eq:low-degree-encoding-definition` and `def:indicator-vector` in the
    75	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`, paper origin
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    77	It is a proof obligation in stage 4.1.
    78	-/
    79	theorem lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    80	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) :
    81	    lowDegreeEnc a x = dotProduct a (indicatorVec x) := by
    82	  sorry
    83	
    84	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Finite-field bases and the fixed binary representation
     5	
     6	The Pauli basis test uses fields of size `2^k` for odd `k`, together with a
     7	chosen self-dual normal basis over `ZMod 2`.  This file records that choice as
     8	data, while exposing Mathlib's basis and algebra-trace APIs for later proofs.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The declarations correspond to `def:admissible-size`, `def:subfields-kappa`,
    13	`def:subfield-trace`, and `def:binary-representation` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:182-232` and `298-315`.
    15	Their paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:433-502,653-728`.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	open scoped BigOperators
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	/-- `IsAdmissibleSize q` is the predicate `q = 2^k` for an odd exponent.
    23	This is `def:admissible-size` in the blueprint
    24	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:210-212`, with paper origin
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:662-667`.
    26	-/
    27	def IsAdmissibleSize (q : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ k : ℕ, Odd k ∧ q = 2 ^ k
    28	
    29	/--
    30	A fixed finite-field model records the carrier and the chosen coding of its
    31	elements by `Fin q`.  The algebra structure and stored basis data make explicit
    32	the paper's once-and-for-all self-dual normal-basis convention; they are
    33	deliberately part of the model rather than quantified afresh by the soundness
    34	theorem.  This is the Lean carrier for `def:binary-representation`, blueprint
    35	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`, paper origin
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-728`.
    37	-/
    38	/- The finite-field carrier is specialized to `Type 0`, as are the finite
    39	models used by the surrounding Euclidean-space API. -/
    40	structure FixedFieldModel (q : ℕ) extends MIPStarRE.LDT.FieldModel.{0} q where
    41	  /-- Scalar restriction from `ZMod 2` to the chosen field. -/
    42	  algebra : Algebra (ZMod 2) K
    43	  /-- Dimension of the chosen basis over the prime subfield. -/
    44	  basisDim : ℕ
    45	  /-- The chosen basis dimension is odd, as required for a self-dual normal basis
    46	  over the binary field. -/
    47	  basisDimOdd : Odd basisDim
    48	  /-- The admissible field-size relation for the chosen basis dimension. -/
    49	  basisCard : q = 2 ^ basisDim
    50	  /-- The chosen basis of `K` over `ZMod 2`. -/
    51	  basis : Module.Basis (Fin basisDim) (ZMod 2) K
    52	  /--
    53	  The inherited coding of `K` is the natural binary encoding of the stored
    54	  basis coordinates.  This field records the source's `downsize` convention
    55	  rather than allowing an unrelated permutation of `Fin q`.  It is the
    56	  coordinate clause of `def:binary-representation` in
    57	  `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`, with paper origin
    58	  `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:669-680`.
    59	  -/
    60	  representation_natural :
    61	    ∀ v : Fin basisDim → ZMod 2,
    62	      (toFieldModel.equiv (basis.equivFun.symm v)).val =
    63	        ∑ i : Fin basisDim, if v i = 1 then 2 ^ i.1 else 0
    64	  /-- Self-duality of the chosen basis with respect to the field trace. -/
    65	  selfDual : ∀ i j, Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K (basis i * basis j) =
    66	    if i = j then 1 else 0
    67	  /-- Normality of the chosen basis, recorded by a Frobenius generator. -/
    68	  normal : ∃ α : K, ∀ i, basis i = α ^ (2 ^ i.1)
    69	
    70	/-!
    71	The paper fixes the field representation and self-dual normal basis once for
    72	each admissible field size.  We expose that choice through a single global
    73	selector rather than carrying a potentially different model in every game
    74	parameter record.  Existence is a named stage-4.3 proof obligation; the
    75	selector itself is the resulting noncomputable choice.
    76	-/
    77	
    78	/-- An admissible binary field size admits the fixed self-dual normal model used
    79	by the Pauli basis test.  This is the existence assertion implicit in
    80	`def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis` and `def:binary-representation`, blueprint
    81	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:234-246,298-315`, paper origin
    82	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680,702-725`.
    83	
    84	The construction of the basis and its natural coding is deferred to the
    85	algebra stage; keeping it as a named theorem makes the proof obligation visible
    86	without adding a model hypothesis to the source-facing test statements.
    87	-/
    88	theorem exists_fixed_field_model (q : ℕ) (hq : IsAdmissibleSize q) :
    89	    Nonempty (FixedFieldModel q) := by
    90	  sorry
    91	
    92	/-- The once-and-for-all field model selected for an admissible size.  Every
    93	QPBT parameter record uses this same choice, matching the paper's fixed
    94	self-dual normal-basis identification rather than quantifying over arbitrary
    95	representations.  Blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`; paper origin
    96	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680`.
    97	-/
    98	noncomputable def fixedFieldModel (q : ℕ) (hq : IsAdmissibleSize q) :
    99	    FixedFieldModel q :=
   100	  Classical.choice (exists_fixed_field_model q hq)
   101	
   102	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Field F.K := F.toFieldModel.instField
   103	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Fintype F.K := F.toFieldModel.instFintype
   104	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : DecidableEq F.K := F.toFieldModel.instDecidableEq
   105	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Algebra (ZMod 2) F.K := F.algebra
   106	
   107	/-- The fixed binary representation obtained from the chosen basis coordinates. -/
   108	noncomputable def binaryRepresentation {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : F.K ≃ Fin q :=
   109	  F.toFieldModel.equiv
   110	
   111	/--
   112	The coordinate map associated with a finite basis.  This is the `κ` of
   113	`def:subfields-kappa` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:182-208`,
   114	whose paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:433-502`.
   115	-/
   116	noncomputable abbrev kappa {F K ι : Type*} [CommSemiring F] [Semiring K]
   117	    [Algebra F K] [Finite ι]
   118	    (b : Module.Basis ι F K) : K ≃ₗ[F] (ι → F) :=
   119	  b.equivFun
   120	
   121	/--
   122	Multiplication by `a` in basis coordinates, using Mathlib's
   123	`Algebra.leftMulMatrix`.  It is the multiplication table `K_a` in
   124	`def:subfields-kappa` (blueprint lines 196-199; paper
   125	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:481-502`).
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable abbrev multiplicationTable {F K ι : Type*} [CommSemiring F]
   128	    [Semiring K] [Algebra F K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   129	    (b : Module.Basis ι F K) : K →ₐ[F] Matrix ι ι F :=
   130	  Algebra.leftMulMatrix b
   131	
   132	/--
   133	The finite-field trace used by the Pauli phases.  This is a thin wrapper around
   134	Mathlib's basis-independent `Algebra.trace`, matching `def:subfield-trace` and
   135	Equation `eq:def-trace` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:217-232`
   136	(`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:481-502`).
   137	-/
   138	noncomputable abbrev binTrace (K : Type*) [CommRing K] [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] :
   139	    K →ₗ[ZMod 2] ZMod 2 :=
   140	  Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K
   141	
   142	/-- The trace selected by a fixed model; this is the map denoted `tr` in the
   143	paper's `def:binary-representation`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`,
   144	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680`. -/
   145	noncomputable def fixedBinTrace {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : F.K → ZMod 2 :=
   146	  binTrace F.K
   147	
   148	/--
   149	The matrix-trace presentation of `fixedBinTrace`, a statement-level bridge to
   150	Equation `eq:def-trace`.  It is the trace assertion in `def:subfield-trace`,
   151	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:217-232`, paper origin
   152	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:481-502`.  Mathlib's
   153	`Algebra.trace_eq_matrix_trace` supplies the basis-independent equality.
   154	-/
   155	theorem fixedBinTrace_eq_matrixTrace {q ι : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q)
   156	    (b : Module.Basis (Fin ι) (ZMod 2) F.K) (a : F.K) :
   157	    fixedBinTrace F a = (multiplicationTable b a).trace := by
   158	  exact Algebra.trace_eq_matrix_trace b a
   159	
   160	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     2	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Basic
     3	
     4	/-!
     5	# Generalized Pauli operators and EPR states
     6	
     7	The definitions here use finite matrix entries and rank-one projectors, so they
     8	are usable by the later game statements without introducing an abstract
     9	operator algebra.  The Fourier/orthogonality identities are retained as named
    10	proof obligations for subsequent stages.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The source-facing nodes are `def:lin-reg`, `def:EPR`, `def:generalized-pauli`,
    15	and `lem:pauli-observable-expansion` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:494-652`.  The paper origin is
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-1161`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    27	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]
    28	
    29	/-- The two generalized Pauli bases used by the test in `def:generalized-pauli`,
    30	blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    31	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    32	-/
    33	inductive PauliKind where
    34	  | X
    35	  | Z
    36	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    37	
    38	/-- The binary character used for generalized Pauli phases; see
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1081`.
    40	
    41	It is public because the Fourier expansion declarations below expose this
    42	character in their statement types. -/
    43	noncomputable def phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    44	  if t = 0 then 1 else -1
    45	
    46	/--
    47	The shift operator `τ^X(a)`.  Blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`,
    48	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`; paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    50	-/
    51	noncomputable def tauShift (a : K) : Op K :=
    52	  fun i j => if i = j + a then 1 else 0
    53	
    54	/--
    55	The phase operator `τ^Z(b)`, with the fixed binary trace in the phase.  It is
    56	the second operator of `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 529-571; paper
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`).
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def tauPhase (b : K) : Op K :=
    60	  fun i j => if i = j then phaseSign (binTrace K (b * j)) else 0
    61	
    62	/-- The single-qudit eigenvector coordinate used in the tensor-product basis;
    63	see `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1126-1161`. -/
    64	private noncomputable def singlePauliVec (W : PauliKind) (e x : K) : ℂ :=
    65	  match W with
    66	  | .Z => if x = e then 1 else 0
    67	  | .X =>
    68	      (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * phaseSign (binTrace K (e * x))
    69	
    70	/--
    71	The normalized single/multi-qudit eigenvector for a Pauli basis label.  For an
    72	index type `ι`, the input `e : ι → K` labels the tensor-product basis vector.
    73	This is the vector form of `def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint
    74	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:550-570`, paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`.
    76	-/
    77	noncomputable def pauliVec {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    78	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) (x : ι → K) : ℂ :=
    79	  ∏ i : ι, singlePauliVec W (e i) (x i)
    80	
    81	/--
    82	The rank-one projector onto `pauliVec W e`.  This is the projective measurement
    83	element `τ^W_e` in `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 562-570; paper
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`).
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    87	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    88	  Matrix.vecMulVec (pauliVec W e) (fun x => star (pauliVec W e x))
    89	
    90	/-- A compact operator-valued form of a generalized Pauli observable from
    91	`def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    93	-/
    94	noncomputable def tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    95	    (W : PauliKind) (a : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    96	  fun x y =>
    97	    ∏ i : ι,
    98	      match W with
    99	      | .X => tauShift (a i) (x i) (y i)
   100	      | .Z => tauPhase (a i) (x i) (y i)
   101	
   102	/--
   103	The EPR vector on a finite label space.  Blueprint `def:EPR`,
   104	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper origin
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
   106	-/
   107	noncomputable def eprState (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
   108	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (V × V) :=
   109	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (V × V) ℂ).symm
   110	    (fun p : V × V =>
   111	      if p.1 = p.2 then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0)
   112	
   113	/-- The EPR vector is normalized on a nonempty finite carrier; see
   114	`def:EPR`, `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`. -/
   115	theorem eprState_norm (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
   116	    ‖eprState V‖ = 1 := by

   216	
   217	We introduce several distance measures that are used throughout.
   218	
   219	\begin{definition}[Distance between states]
   220	  \label{def:state-distance}

   222		Let $\{\ket{\psi_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ and $\{\ket{\psi'_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ be two
   223	  families of states in the same space $\mH$.

   225	  $\{ \ket{\psi'_n} \}$ are \emph{$\delta$-close}, denoted as $\ket{\psi}

   227	  O(\delta(n))$.

   229	  on the indexing parameter $n$ implicit, writing e.g.\ $\ket{\psi}$ for $\ket{\psi_n}$.)

   233	  \label{def:consistency}

The $O(\cdot)$ is taken as $n\to\infty$.}

   378	where all expectations are taken according to $\mu$.

   406	The following lemma ensures that, when two families of measurements are close on a

   410	\begin{lemma}
   411	  \label{lem:commutation-analysis}
   412	  Let $\{A^x_{a,\, b}\}$, $\{B^x_{a,\, b,\, c}\}$, $\{C^x_{a,\, c}\}$ be POVMs.
   413	  Suppose $\{B^x_{a,\, b,\, c}\}$ is projective, and
   414	  \begin{align*}
   415	    A^x_{a,\, b} \otimes \Id_\bob &\approx_\delta \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, b}\;,\\
   416	    C^x_{a,\, c} \otimes \Id_\bob &\approx_\delta \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, c}\;,
   417	  \end{align*}
   418		where recall that $B^x_{a,\, b} = \sum_c B^x_{a,b,c}$ and similarly $B^x_{a,\, c}=\sum_b B^x_{a,b,c}$. 
   419	  Then the following approximate commutation relation holds:
   420	  \begin{equation*}
   421	    [A^x_{a,\, b}, C^x_{a,\, c}] \otimes I_\bob \approx_\delta 0\;.
   422	  \end{equation*}

   427	  \approx_\delta \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, c}$ and $\{A^x_{a,b} \otimes
   428	  \Id_\bob \}$, we have
   429	  \begin{equation}
   430	    \label{eq:commutation-analysis-1}
   455	    \label{eq:commutation-analysis-4}
   456	    C^x_{a,\, c} A^x_{a,\, b} \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\delta
   457	    \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, b,\, c}\,.

   465	The following lemma is a slightly modified version of~\cite[Fact~4.34]{NW19}.
   466	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:ld-sandwich}
   467	  Let $k \geq 0$ be an integer and let $\eps>0$.
   468	  Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution over $\mX$.
   469	  For each $1 \leq i \leq k$ let $\mG_i$ be a finite set of functions $g_i : \mY
   470	  \rightarrow \mR_i$ and for each $x \in \mX$ let $\{G^{i,\, x}_g\}_{g\in
   471	    \mG_i}$ be a projective measurement.
   472	  Suppose that for all $i\in \{1,\ldots,k\}$, $\mG_i$ satisfies the following
   473	  property: for any two $g_i \neq g_i' \in \mG_i$, the probability that $g_i(y)
   474	  = g_i'(y)$ over a uniformly random $y \in \mY$ is at most $\eps$.
   475	
   476	  Let $\bigl\{ A^{x}_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_k} \bigr\}$ be a projective
   477	  measurement with outcomes $(g_1,\ldots,g_k) \in \mG_1\times\cdots\times
   478	  \mG_k$.
   479	  For each $1 \leq i \leq k$, suppose that on average over $x \sim \mu$ and
   480	  $y\in \mY$ sampled uniformly at random,
   481	  \begin{equation}\label{eq:ld-sandwich-1}
   482	    A^{x}_{[\eval_y(\cdot)_i = a_i]} \abc G^{i,\, x}_{[\eval_y(\cdot)=a_i]}\;.
   483	  \end{equation}
   484	  Define the POVM family $\{C^x_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_k}\}$, for $x\in \mX$, by
   485	  \begin{equation*}
   486	    C^x_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_k} = G^{k,\, x}_{g_1} \cdots
   487	    G^{2,\, x}_{g_{k-1}} \, G^{1,\, x}_{g_k} \, G^{2,\, x}_{g_{k-1}} \cdots
   488	    G^{k,\, x}_{g_1}\;.
   489	  \end{equation*}
   490	  Then on average over $x\sim \mu$ and $y\in \mY$ sampled uniformly at random,
   491	  \begin{equation}\label{eq:ld-sandwich-2}
   492	    A^x_{[\eval_y(\cdot) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots,\, a_k)]} \abc[k(\delta+\eps)^{1/2}]
   493	    C^x_{[\eval_y(\cdot) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots,\, a_k)]}\;.
   494	\end{equation}
   495	\end{lemma}

   497	\begin{proof}
   498	  The proof is identical to the one given in \cite[Fact~4.34]{NW19}, with the
   499	  only modification needed to insert the dependence on $x$ for all measurements
   500	  considered.

   505	Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a distribution on $(x,y_1,y_2)\in \mathcal{X}\times \mathcal{Y}_1\times \mathcal{Y}_2$. For $i\in \{1,2\}$ let $\mathcal{G}_i$ be a collection of functions $g_i: \mathcal{Y}_i \to \mathcal{R}_i$ and let $\{(G_i)^{x}_{g}\}_{g\in \mathcal{G}_i}$ be families of measurements such that $\{(G_2)^x_g\}_g$ is projective for every $x$. Suppose further that for every $(x,y_1)$ it holds that for $g_2\neq g'_2 \in \mathcal{G}_2$ the probability, on average over $y_2$ chosen from $\mathcal{D}$ conditioned on $(x,y_1)$, that $g_2(y_2)=g'_2(y_2)$  is at most $\eta$. 
   506	Let $\{A^{x,y_1,y_2}_{a_1,a_2}\}$ be a family of projective measurements with outcomes $(a_1,a_2)\in \mathcal{R}_1 \times \mathcal{R}_2$ such that for $i\in \{1,2\}$,
   507	\begin{equation}\label{eq:pasting-1}

   509	\end{equation}
   510	and 
   511	\begin{equation}\label{eq:pasting-2}

   541	\subsection{The class $\MIP^*$}
   542	
   543	The complexity class $\MIP^*$ of \emph{multi-prover interactive proof
   544	  systems with entangled provers} is the class of languages that can be
   545	decided by a \emph{proof system} in which a polynomial-time classical
   546	\emph{verifier} interacts with noncommunicating, computationally unbounded
   547	 \emph{provers} who may share a \emph{finite-dimensional} entangled state. In general there may be polynomially many provers,
   548	and the verifier may interact with them over polynomially many
   549	rounds. In each round, the verifier generates a question for
   550	each prover and receives a response from them. At the end of
   551	the interaction the verifier 
   552	decides to either accept or reject. A language $L$ is in $\MIP^*$ if for
   553	every input $z \in L$, there exists a strategy that the provers can
   554	use to convince the verifier to accept with high probability ($\geq 2/3$), and for every input $z \not\in L$, there is
   555	\emph{no} strategy that the provers can use to convince the verifier

60	\begin{remark}
    61	  Unless specified otherwise, all strategies considered in this paper are tensor
    62	  product strategies, and we simply call them \emph{strategies}.
    63	  Similarly, we refer to $\val^*(\game)$ as the \emph{value} of the game
    64	  $\game$.
    65	\end{remark}
    66	
    67	
    68	\begin{definition}[Projective strategies]
    69	  \label{def:projective-strategy}
    70	  We say that a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ is \emph{projective} if
    71	  all the measurements $\{A^x_a\}_a$ and $\{B^y_b\}_b$ are projective.
    72	\end{definition}
    73	
    74	\begin{definition}\label{rem:symmetric-games}
    75		A game $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is
    76	  \emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both
    77	  players (i.e.\
    78	  $\cal{X} = \cal{Y}$ and $\cal{A} = \cal{B}$), the distribution $\mu$ is
    79	  symmetric (i.e.\
    80	  $\mu(x,y) = \mu(y,x)$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players
    81	  symmetrically (i.e.\ for all $x,y,a,b$, $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$).
    82	 
    83	We call a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$
    84	  \emph{symmetric} if $\ket{\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\mH \otimes \mH$, for some
    85	  Hilbert space $\mH$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors,
    86	  and the measurement operators of both players are identical.
    87	\end{definition}
    88	
    89	We often specify symmetric games $\game$ and symmetric strategies $\strategy$ using
    90	  a compact notation: we write $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ and
    91	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ where $M$ denotes the set of measurement
    92	  operators for both players.
    93	
    94	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:symmetric-strat}
    95	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A},  \mu, D)$ be a symmetric game
    96	  such that $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some $\eps\geq 0$.
    97	  Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy
    98	  $\strategy=(\ket{\psi},M)$ such that $\val^*(\game,\strategy)\geq 1-\eps$.
    99	\end{lemma}
   100	
   101	\begin{proof}
   102	  By definition for any $\eps'>\eps$ there exists a strategy $\strategy'= (\ket{\psi'},A,B)$ such
   103	  that $\val^*(\game,\strategy')\geq 1-\eps'$.
   104	Using Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}) we can assume
   105	without loss of generality that $\ket{\psi'}\in\C_{\alice'}^d\otimes \C_{\bob'}^d$ for some integer $d$
   106	  and that for every $x$, $A^x$ and $B^x$ are projective measurements.
   107	Let
   108	  \[
   109	    \ket{\psi} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \big( \ket{0}_\alice \ket{1}_\bob
   110	    \ket{\psi'}_{\alice'\bob'} + \ket{1}_\alice \ket{0}_\bob
   111	    \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{\alice'\bob'}\big) \in (\C_{\alice}^2 \otimes
   112	    \C_{\alice'}^d) \otimes (\C_\bob^2 \otimes \C_{\bob'}^d)\;,
   113	  \]
   114	  where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ is obtained from $\ket{\psi}$ by permuting the two
   115	  players' registers.
   116	  Observe that $\ket{\psi}$ is invariant under permutation of $\alice\alice'$
   117	  and $\bob\bob'$.
   118	
   119	  For any question $x\in \cal{X}$ define the measurement $M^x = \{M^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$
   120	  acting on the Hilbert space $\C^2 \otimes \C^d$ as follows:
   121	  \[
   122	  	M^x_a = \ketbra{0}{0} \otimes A^x_a + \ketbra{1}{1} \otimes B^x_a \;,
   123	  \]
   124		i.e.\ for $\ket{\varphi} \in \C^d$, $M^x_a(\ket{0}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{0}A^x_a\ket{\varphi}$ and $M^x_a(\ket{1}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{1}B^x_a\ket{\varphi}$.
   125	  When Alice receives question $x$, she measures $M^x$ on registers $\alice \alice'$, and when Bob receives 
   126	  question $y$, he measures $M^y$ on registers $\bob \bob'$.
   127	Using that by assumption the decision predicate $D$ for $\game$ is symmetric,
   128	  it is not hard to verify that $\val^*(\game,\strategy) =
   129	  \val^*(\game,\strategy')$.
   130	\end{proof}
   131	
   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:comm-strategy}
   134	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a game, and let
   135	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy for $\game$ such that  $\mH_A = \mH_B$.
   136	  Let $S \subseteq \cal{X} \times \cal{Y}$ denote the support of the question
   137	  distribution $\mu$, i.e.\ the set of $(x,y)$ such that $\mu(x,y)>0$.
   138	  We say that $\strategy$ is a \emph{commuting strategy for $\game$} if for all
   139	  question pairs $(x, y) \in S$, we have $[A^x_a, B^y_b] = 0$ 
   140	  for all $a
   141	  \in \cal{A}, b \in \cal{B}$, where $[A, B] = AB - BA$ denotes the commutator.
   142	\end{definition}
   143	
   144	\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]
   145	  \label{def:consistent-measurement}
   146	  Let $\cal{A}$ be a finite set, let $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$ be a
   147	  state, and let $\{ M_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ be a projective measurement on
   148	  $\mH$.
   149	  We say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$} if
   150	  and only if
   151	  \begin{equation*}
   152	    \forall a \in \mA\;,\quad M_a \otimes \Id_\bob\, \ket{\psi}
   153	    = \Id_\alice \otimes M_a\, \ket{\psi}\;.
   154	  \end{equation*}
   155		When the state $\ket{\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent}.
   156	\end{definition}
   157	
   158	The terminology ``consistent'' arises from the fact that when the measurement $\{M_a\}$ is performed on both registers of $\ket{\psi}$, the probability of obtaining twice the same outcome is 
   159	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes (M_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} \,=\,1\;,\]
   160	where the first equality is by definition of consistency, the second uses that $\{M_a\}$ is projective, and the last uses $\sum_a M_a=\Id$. 
   161	
   162	\begin{definition}[Consistent strategies]
   163	  \label{def:consistent-strategy}
   164		Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a projective strategy with state
   165	  $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$, for some Hilbert space~$\mH$, which is
   166	  defined on question alphabets $\cal{X}$ and~$\cal{Y}$ and answer alphabets
   167	  $\cal{A}$ and~$\cal{B}$, respectively.
   168	  We say that the strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{consistent} if for all $x \in
   169	  \cal{X}$, the measurement $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on
   170	  $\ket{\psi}$ and if for all $y \in \cal{Y}$, the measurement $\{B^y_b\}_{b \in
   171	    \cal{B}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$.
   172	\end{definition}
   173	
   174	We almost always restrict our attention to symmetric strategies. In this case, consistency implies that whenever both players are sent the same question, they provide the same answer. 
   175	
   176	\begin{definition}
   177	  \label{def:spcc}
   178	  We say that a strategy $\strategy$ for a game $\game$ is \emph{PCC} if it is projective, consistent, and commuting for $\game$.
   179	  Additionally, we say that a PCC strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{SPCC} if it is furthermore symmetric.
   180	\end{definition}
   181	
   182	
   183	Recall that for a (pure) state $\ket{\psi}\in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$, the \emph{Schmidt rank} of $\ket{\psi}$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that 
   184	\[ \ket{\psi} = \sum_{i=1}^k\, \alpha_i \ket{u_i}\otimes \ket{v_i}\;,\]
   185	for some orthonormal families $\{\ket{u_i}\}\subset \mH_\alice$ and $\{\ket{v_i}\}\subset\mH_\bob$ and $\alpha_i>0$. The coefficients $\alpha_i$ are uniquely defined by $\ket{\psi}$ and called \emph{Schmidt coefficients}. The state $\ket{\psi}$ is called \emph{maximally entangled} if $\alpha_i=\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}}$ for all $i=1,\ldots,k$.

    18	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    19	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    20	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    24	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    25	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    27	      if a = b then 0 else
    28	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    29	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)
    30	
    31	/-- The quantitative relation in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    32	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    33	def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
    34	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    36	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    37	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
    38	  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ
    39	
    40	/-- Unit-alphabet specialization of `def:povm-distance`, blueprint
    41	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    42	noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    43	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    45	  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ
    46	
    47	/-- The unit-alphabet operator distance equals its one-outcome family form from
    48	`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper
    49	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    50	theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    51	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    52	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    53	    opDistSq μ M N ψ = opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x)
    54	      (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ := rfl
    55	
    56	/-- The strategy-distance relation `def:strategy-distance`. The two strategies'
    57	local Hilbert spaces are identified, and both measurement distances are
    58	evaluated on the first strategy's state. Blueprint
    59	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    60	structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game) (S S' : Strategy G) (δ : ℝ) : Prop where
    61	  /-- Identification of Alice's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    62	  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA
    63	  /-- Identification of Bob's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    64	  hB : S.ιB = S'.ιB
    65	  state : stateDistSq S.ψ (reindexState
    66	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hA).symm (Equiv.cast hB).symm) S'.ψ) ≤ δ
    67	  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
    68	      (fun x a => heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1)
    69	      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hA) ((S'.A x).effect a)) 1)
    70	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    71	  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
    72	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b))
    73	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hB) ((S'.B y).effect b)))
    74	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    75

     2	\label{sec:prelim}
     3	
     4	\paragraph{Notation.}
     5	We use $\Sigma$ to denote a finite alphabet.
     6	$\N$ is the set of positive integers.
     7	For $w\in\{0,1\}$, $\overline{w}$ denotes $1-w$.
     8	For $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, $\overline{w}=\bob$ if $w=\alice$ and
     9	$\overline{w}=\alice$ otherwise.
    10	(For notational convenience we often implicitly make the identifications
    11	$1\leftrightarrow \alice$ and $2\leftrightarrow \bob$.)
    12	We use $\F$ to denote a finite field.
    13	We write $M_n(\F)$ to denote the set of $n\times n$ matrices over $\F$.
    14	We write $I$ to denote the identity operator on a vector space.
    15	We write $\Tr(\cdot)$ for the matrix trace.
    16	We write $\mH$ to denote a separable Hilbert space.
    17	For a linear operator $T$, $\|T\|$ denotes the operator norm.
    18	
    19	\paragraph{Asymptotics.}
    20	All logarithms are base $2$.
    21	We use the notation $O(\cdot)$, $\poly(\cdot)$, and $\polylog(\cdot)$ in the
    22	following way.
    23	For $f,g:\N\to\R_+$ we write $f(n)=O(g(n))$ (omitting the integer $n$ when it is
    24	clear from context) to mean that there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for all
    25	$n\in\N$, $f(n)\leq C g(n)$.
    26	When we write $f(a_1,\ldots,a_k) = \poly(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$, this indicates that
    27	there exists a universal constant $C > 0$ (which may vary each time the notation
    28	is used in the paper) such that $f(a_1,\ldots,a_k) \leq C( a_1 \cdots a_k)^C$
    29	for all positive $a_1,\ldots,a_k$.
    30	Similarly, when we write $f(a_1,\ldots,a_k) = \polylog(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$, there
    31	exists a universal constant $C$ such that $f(a_1,\ldots,a_k) \leq C\prod_{i =
    32	  1}^k \log^C (1+ a_i)$ for all positive $a_1,\ldots,a_k$.
    33	Finally, we write $\log(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$ as short hand for $\prod_{i = 1}^k \log
    34	(1 + a_i)$.\footnote{The additional $1$ in the argument of the $\log(\cdot)$ is
    35	  to ensure that this quantity is strictly positive.}
    36	
    37	\subsection{Turing machines}
    38	\label{sec:tms}
    39	
    40	Turing machines are a model of computation introduced
    41	in~\cite{turing1937computable}, and play a central role in our modeling of verifiers for nonlocal
    42	games. Here we give an overview of certain aspects of Turing machines that are relevant for
    43	this paper. For an in-depth treatment of Turing machines, we refer the reader to the textbooks of 
    44	Papadimitriou~\cite{Pap94} or Sipser~\cite{sipser2012introduction}.
    45	
    46	The tapes of a Turing machine are infinite one-dimensional arrays of cells that
    47	are indexed by natural numbers.
    48	A \emph{$k$-input} Turing machine $\cal{M}$ has $k$ input tapes, one work tape,
    49	and one output tape. 
    50	Each cell of a tape has symbols taken either from the set $\{0,1\}$ or the blank

     4	
     5	Shared quantitative predicates for the polynomial-error bounds in QPBT

    18	14--15. One universal positive constant is both the prefactor and exponent, as
    19	in `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:26-29`. -/
    20	def IsPolyErr (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
    21	  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x, 0 < x →
    22	    0 ≤ f x ∧ f x ≤ C * Real.rpow x C
    23	
    24	/-- The two-parameter polynomial bound used by `lem:pasting`: on positive
    25	arguments, one universal positive constant is both the prefactor and exponent.

    27	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:518-524`; blueprint
    28	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:442-469`. -/
    29	def IsPolyErr₂ (f : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
    30	  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x y, 0 < x → 0 < y →
    31	    0 ≤ f x y ∧ f x y ≤ C * Real.rpow (x * y) C
    32	
    33	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    31	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:442-469`. -/

   240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and

   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}

   612	The following theorem records the self-testing (also known as \emph{rigidity})
   613	properties of the Magic Square game.
   614	Its self-testing properties
   615	are crucial to the Pauli basis test.
   616	In particular, it is used to enforce anticommutation relations between certain
   617	pairs of operators.
   618	We will refer to this theorem in the proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test (\Cref{thm:pauli} below) in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}.
   619	
   620	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]
   621	  \label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   622	
   623	
   624	Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ with probability $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ is a state. Then there exist local isometries $\phi_A: \mH_A \to \mH_{A'} \otimes \mH_{A''},\phi_B: \mH_B \to \mH_{B'} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ (where $\mH_{A'},\mH_{B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\otimes 2}$ and $\mH_{A''},\mH_{B''}$ are finite dimensional) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{A''} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ such that 
   625	\begin{enumerate}
   626	    \item $\left \| \phi_A \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2} \otimes \ket{\aux} \right \| \leq O(\sqrt{\eps})$,
   627	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have that
   628	    \begin{gather*}
   629	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^X_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   630	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^Z_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   631	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^X_b)_{B'} \\
   632	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^Z_b)_{B'}
   633	    \end{gather*}
   634	    where the $\approx_{\sqrt{\eps}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}_{A'B'} \otimes \ket{\aux}_{A''B''}$ and the answer summation is over $b \in \{0,1\}$. As a consequence, letting 
   635	    \begin{gather*}
   636	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_1 \\
   637	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_1 \\
   638	    \end{gather*}
   639	    it holds that
   640	    \begin{gather*}
   641	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} \otimes I_{B' B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \otimes I_{B' B''} \\
   642	        I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \;,
   643	      \end{gather*}
   644	      where the notation $M \approx_{\delta} N$ for $M, N$ that are not POVM
   645	      elements means
   646	      \[  \bra{\psi} (M-N)^\dagger (M-N) \ket{\psi}  \leq  O(\delta). \]
   647	\end{enumerate}
   648	
   649	\end{theorem}
   650	\begin{proof}
   651	 	A proof of the rigidity of the Magic Square game can be found in~\cite[Theorem 6.9]{coladangelo2017robust}. There are a couple minor differences between their rigidity statement and the one stated here. First, they state that the robustness of the Magic Square self-test is $O(\eps)$; however they specify the closeness between the actual and ideal states in terms of the trace norm, whereas we specify the closeness between $\phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi}$ and $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}\otimes \ket{\aux}$ in terms of the Euclidean distance, which translates to $O(\sqrt{\eps})$ instead of $O(\eps)$. Second, their choice of ideal strategy specifies that the observables corresponding to $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$ questions are $I \otimes \sigma^Z$ and $\sigma^{Z} \sigma^{X} \otimes \sigma^Z \sigma^X$; however under a local change of basis these are equivalent to $\sigma^X \otimes I$ and $\sigma^Z \otimes I$ respectively.
   652	\end{proof}
   653	
   654	We will need the following theorem,
   655	which shows that any pair of anticommuting observables 
   656	can be used to form a value-$1$ strategy for the Magic Square game.
   657	
   658	\begin{theorem}
   659	  \label{thm:ms-from-ac}
   660	  Let $A = \{A_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ and $B = \{B_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ be two-outcome
   661	  projective measurements acting on $(\C^q)^{\otimes n}$ which are consistent on
   662	  $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes n}$, and let $\mathcal{O}_A = A_0 - A_1$ and
   663	  $\mathcal{O}_B = B_0 - B_1$ be the corresponding observables.
   664	  Suppose that $\mathcal{O}_A \mathcal{O}_B = -\mathcal{O}_B \mathcal{O}_A$.
   665	  Then there exists a symmetric strategy $\strategy = (\psi, M)$ for the Magic
   666	  Square game with the following properties.
   667	  \begin{enumerate}
   668	  \item $\strategy$ is an SPCC strategy of value $1$.
   669	  \item The state $\ket{\psi}$ has the form $\ket{\psi} = \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes
   670	      n} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}$.
   671	  \item For $b \in \{0,1\}$, we have $M^{\Variable_1}_b = A_b \otimes I$ and
   672	    $M^{\Variable_5}_b = B_b \otimes I$.\label{item:embeds}
   673	  \end{enumerate}
   674	\end{theorem}
   675	
   676	\begin{proof}
   677	  The strategy~$\strategy$ is based on the canonical two-qubit strategy for the
   678	  Magic Square game as described in, for example,~\cite{aravind2002simple}.
   679	  The state is $\ket{\psi} = \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes n} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}$.
   680	  We specify the measurements of~$\strategy$ in
   681	  Figure~\ref{fig:ms-operator-soln} as an \emph{operator solution} for the Magic
   682	  Square game, meant to be read as follows: each cell contains a two-outcome
   683	  projective measurement $\{E_0, E_1\}$ on $(\C^q)^{\otimes n} \otimes \C^2$
   684	  written as its \emph{$\pm 1$-valued observable} $E_0 - E_1$.
   685	  When Player~$\alice$ or~$\bob$ receives the question $\Variable_j$ for $j \in
   686	  \{1, \ldots, 9\}$, they measure their share of~$\ket{\psi}$ using the
   687	  measurement specified by the cell corresponding to~$\Variable_j$ and receive a
   688	  single-bit measurement.
   689	  When they receive the question $\Constraint_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,6\}$,
   690	  they simultaneously perform the three measurements in the corresponding row or
   691	  column on $\ket{\psi}$ to obtain three bits.
   692	  For example, if Player~$\alice$ receives question~$\Variable_1$, they
   693	  measure~$\ket{\psi}$ using the measurement $\{A_0 \otimes I, A_1 \otimes I\}$
   694	  corresponding to the observable $\cal{O}_A \otimes I$ (where the first
   695	  operator acts on $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes n}$ and the second acts on
   696	  $\ket{\EPR_2}$).
   697	  Similarly, on question~$\Variable_5$, they use the measurement $\{B_0 \otimes
   698	  I, B_1 \otimes I\}$.
   699	  This establishes Item~\ref{item:embeds} of the theorem.

   595	\label{sec:types}
   596	
   597	The question distribution of the Pauli basis test is \emph{typed}: each question is a pair consisting of a type, drawn together with the other player's type from the edges of a fixed \emph{type graph}, and a question content, drawn from a CL distribution determined by the pair of types.

   599	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]\label{def:typed-cl-functions}
   600		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsTypedCondLinearFamily}
   601		\leanok
   602		\uses{def:cl-func}
   603		Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite set (the \emph{type set}) and let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \ge 0$. A \emph{$\mathcal T$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_t\}_{t \in \mathcal T}$ such that, for each $t \in \mathcal T$, $L_t$ is an $\ell$-level conditionally linear function on $V$.
   604	\end{definition}
   605	
   606	% Nonemptiness of the edge set is stated explicitly here: with E empty, m = k = 0 and the
   607	% normalization 1/(2m-k) below is undefined. The source
   608	% (references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82) leaves this boundary hypothesis implicit.
   609	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]\label{def:graph-distribution}
   610		Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and nonempty edge set $E$. Edges in $E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u = v$ represents a self-loop. Suppose there are $m \ge 1$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops. Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of $G$} is the distribution over $U \times U$ such that for every $(u,v) \in U \times U$,
   611		\[
   612			\mu_G(u, v) =
   613			\begin{cases}
   614				1/(2m-k) & \text{if } \{u,v\} \in E\,,\\
   615				0 & \text{otherwise}\,.
   616			\end{cases}
   617		\]
   618		This is identical to the uniform distribution over ordered pairs $(u,v) \in U \times U$ such that $\{u,v\} \in E$: each edge that is not a self-loop contributes two ordered pairs, and each self-loop contributes one, whence the normalization $2m-k$.

   144	\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]
   145	  \label{def:consistent-measurement}
   146	  Let $\cal{A}$ be a finite set, let $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$ be a
   147	  state, and let $\{ M_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ be a projective measurement on
   148	  $\mH$.
   149	  We say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$} if
   150	  and only if
   151	  \begin{equation*}
   152	    \forall a \in \mA\;,\quad M_a \otimes \Id_\bob\, \ket{\psi}
   153	    = \Id_\alice \otimes M_a\, \ket{\psi}\;.
   154	  \end{equation*}
   155		When the state $\ket{\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent}.
   156	\end{definition}
   157	
   158	The terminology ``consistent'' arises from the fact that when the measurement $\{M_a\}$ is performed on both registers of $\ket{\psi}$, the probability of obtaining twice the same outcome is 
   159	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes (M_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} \,=\,1\;,\]
   160	where the first equality is by definition of consistency, the second uses that $\{M_a\}$ is projective, and the last uses $\sum_a M_a=\Id$. 
   161	
   162	\begin{definition}[Consistent strategies]
   163	  \label{def:consistent-strategy}
   164		Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a projective strategy with state
   165	  $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$, for some Hilbert space~$\mH$, which is
   166	  defined on question alphabets $\cal{X}$ and~$\cal{Y}$ and answer alphabets
   167	  $\cal{A}$ and~$\cal{B}$, respectively.
   168	  We say that the strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{consistent} if for all $x \in
   169	  \cal{X}$, the measurement $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on
   170	  $\ket{\psi}$ and if for all $y \in \cal{Y}$, the measurement $\{B^y_b\}_{b \in
   171	    \cal{B}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$.
   172	\end{definition}
   173	
   174	We almost always restrict our attention to symmetric strategies. In this case, consistency implies that whenever both players are sent the same question, they provide the same answer.
